research_question: What is the effect of adding a long-acting beta2 agonist (LABA) to a medium dose of inhaled corticosteroid (ICS), as a combination inhaler or separate inhalers, compared with the same medium dose of ICS alone, on moderate-to-severe asthma exacerbations in adolescents and adults (aged 12 or over) with uncontrolled asthma despite medium-dose ICS?
outcome_description: Number of participants experiencing at least one moderate or severe asthma exacerbation (defined as requiring systemic corticosteroids, emergency department visit, or hospitalization, or trial-defined moderate/severe exacerbation) out of the total participants randomized in each arm over the treatment period.
positive_direction: Fewer participants experiencing moderate-to-severe asthma exacerbations with medium-dose ICS plus LABA compared to medium-dose ICS alone (RR < 1, favoring combination therapy)
search_queries: asthma medium dose inhaled corticosteroid LABA exacerbation randomized trial
ICS LABA combination versus ICS alone asthma exacerbations controlled trial
budesonide fluticasone formoterol salmeterol moderate severe asthma exacerbation trial
inclusion_criteria: Randomized controlled trials of at least 12 weeks duration in adolescents and adults (aged 12 years or older) with asthma uncontrolled on medium-dose ICS
Comparison between a medium-dose inhaled corticosteroid (ICS) plus a long-acting beta2-agonist (LABA) versus the same medium-dose ICS alone
Quantitative reporting of the number of participants with at least one moderate or severe asthma exacerbation per randomized arm (intention-to-treat)
exclusion_criteria: Not an original empirical randomized controlled trial (systematic reviews, meta-analyses, observational studies, editorials, and review articles are excluded)
No direct comparison between medium-dose ICS plus LABA and the identical medium-dose ICS alone (e.g. trials comparing different baseline ICS doses, high-dose ICS arms, or adding LAMA)

No quantitative event count data for participants with at least one moderate-to-severe asthma exacerbation (e.g. reporting only annualised event rates, rate ratios, or lung function alone without dichotomous event counts)
Studies conducted in pediatric populations under 12 years of age or in populations without asthma (e.g. COPD)
moderators_to_extract: Specific ICS molecule (e.g. fluticasone propionate, budesonide, beclomethasone dipropionate)
Inhaler regimen (fixed-dose single combination inhaler vs separate inhalers)
Trial duration in weeks (e.g. 12 to 24 weeks vs >24 weeks)
Baseline exacerbation history / severity requirements at study entry
effect_size_note: Pool as risk ratio (RR) using a random-effects model, comparing participants with at least one moderate-to-severe exacerbation in the ICS plus LABA arm versus the ICS alone arm (RR < 1 favours combination therapy).
